name: issue_858_comfort_family_reactive_ceiling_breach
description: Issue #858 / #1066 (Design D nearest-edge arming, docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f). Symmetric companion to issue_858_comfort_family_reactive_floor_breach.json: a cool day (classifier hvac_mode=heat), the scenario's only classification event at 06:00, then indoor rises above comfort_cool (72F) through temp_update events alone. The first reading above the ceiling (14:00, 73F) must arm cool immediately, so the switch lands by 14:00.
notes: Occupant impact: an unseasonably warm afternoon pushes a cool-classified (heat-armed) house above the comfort ceiling. The occupant must get cooling on the first reading above the ceiling, not 30 minutes later or after a confirmation wait.

Symmetry: the same reactive wiring that closes the heat-side incident (comfort_family_temperature_check() on every thermostat temperature change) must work for a ceiling breach; Design D's rule is symmetric (indoor > ceiling -> cooling immediately, ignoring the dwell lock). The assertion time bounds are the first breach reading (14:00).
Classification fields: day_type=cool with hvac_mode=heat, windows_recommended=false match classifier.py for DAY_TYPE_COOL.

(a) Scenario effectiveness: reverting the ceiling side of the selector/reactive check (indoor > ceiling) makes this scenario fail exactly as reverting the floor side fails the companion. With nearest-edge arming deleted (origin/main) a cool day is natively heating; cool is against-grain and needs a breach beyond the cool-day deadband, a recency check and a 90 s sustain across two evaluations, so the first reading above the ceiling (14:00) at most arms a candidate and comfort_family_switch_by(cooling, 14:00), comfort_family=cooling and last_hvac_mode=cool would fail.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08 section 6f rule row 'indoor > ceiling -> cooling' and 'Reactive evaluation'.
(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: the house sits above the comfort ceiling with the furnace armed and no cooling for up to 30 minutes per missed cycle.

events.note: Cool-day classification (native heating). Only classification event in this scenario.
First reading above the ceiling: 73F, 1F above comfort_cool(72). Ceiling breach: the reactive check arms cool on this very reading.

assertions.reason: Baseline: cool day, indoor within band -- comfort band arms normally at the floor.
Issue #858 / #1066: the switch to cooling lands on the first breach reading (14:00), driven entirely by the reactive temperature-tick path, symmetric with the floor side.
Final engine state confirms cooling is armed, not merely an emitted event.
The commanded mode is a real climate service call at comfort_cool, not merely an internal flag.

verdict.summary: A ceiling breach arms cool on the first reactive temperature tick, symmetric with the heat-side fix (Issue #858, tightened for Issue #1066).
verdict.observed_behavior: Single classification event at 06:00 (cool/heat); the 73F reading at 14:00 switches the family to cooling and commands cool.
verdict.expected_behavior: The reactive selector is direction-agnostic: above the ceiling means cool immediately.
